# Identify what self-improvement changes: answers, experience, interfaces, and system versions

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-13 · 59 topic entries / 22 representative comparisons

Self-Refine revises the current artifact, Reflexion changes what experience the next attempt can read, HarnessLens checks local workflow changes, Agent S4 evolves interface repositories, RSIFlow chooses the intervention layer, and AgentX brings candidates into a production loop with guardrails. More rounds are not a shared algorithm: persistent state and acceptance rules define what changes. CROP edits system prompts offline and penalizes output cost. EvalAlloc allocates SEARCH evaluations instead of repairing candidate code, estimates fitness against fixed references, and runs paired confirmation.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Mechanism comparison {#comparison}

Axes: Whether the mutable object is an answer, textual experience, interface, model, or artifact · Whether a change serves only the current task or becomes a persistent version · Whether feedback proposes edits, selects parents, accepts candidates, or authorizes release · Whether failures are rolled back, retained in a population, or stored as knowledge

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Separate remembering how to change from actually changing the system

Self-Refine changes the current output; Reflexion persists text for later attempts. Agent S4 versions interface code and knowledge so available observations and actions can change. RSIFlow separates model, workflow, and artifact. Future outcomes may improve in each case, but do not call all of them model learning. Record what changed, how it executes, and what the next task inherits rather than one policy-update count.

Sources: [Self-Refine](../../../../agent-research/2303.17651-self-refine/README-en.md) · [Reflexion](../../../../agent-research/2303.11366-reflexion/README-en.md) · [Evolving Agent Interfaces](../../../../agent-research/2610.28601-agent-s4/README-en.md) · [RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent](../../../../agent-research/2610.21791-rsiflow/README-en.md)

### Population admission, acceptance, and release are distinct

Agent S4 retains temporarily low-scoring descendants for later parent selection, a nongreedy search. RSIFlow changes current state only for valid improvements over the same parent. HarnessLens limits acceptance to attributable behavioral evidence. Production AgentX also requires guardrails. Archiving a candidate, passing local validation, and affecting live traffic are not one 'integrated' status. Compare rules and scope rather than ranking incompatible paper scores.

Sources: [Evolving Agent Interfaces](../../../../agent-research/2610.28601-agent-s4/README-en.md) · [RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent](../../../../agent-research/2610.21791-rsiflow/README-en.md) · [Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification](../../../../agent-research/2608.27311-harnesslens/README-en.md) · [AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems](../../../../agent-research/2606.26859-agentx/README-en.md)

### October 29: New method and source changes

RuHarness does not rank its criterion frontier by one accuracy value. A 2×3 behavior/outcome table yields a Jeffreys–Dirichlet posterior for a conservative utility quantile, while set novelty and redundancy stay fixed from observed traces. This separates finite-sample uncertainty from candidate admission: only active criteria enter the frontier and final harness edits require strictly positive independent validation gains. Local work has no LLM judge or harness generation.

Sources: [Self-Refine](../../../../agent-research/2303.17651-self-refine/README-en.md) · [When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement](../../../../agent-research/2610.36826-ruharness/README-en.md)

### Track edit targets, judging criteria, and evaluation budgets separately

Self-Refine edits the current output. CROP instead uses training feedback to change a general system prompt for later tasks and explicitly charges output tokens; it does not claim model-weight training. RuHarness maintains a rubric frontier that distinguishes current failures. EvalAlloc decides which SEARCH items deserve real evaluation: with fixed item references it completes sparse estimates, fills only unobserved cells with predictions, then confirms on a common prefix with cached results. Rubric utility, predicted fitness, and real held-out success are different evidence. Half the cells does not mean half the LLM cost.

Sources: [CROP: Token-Efficient Reasoning in Large Language Models via Regularized Prompt Optimization](../../../../agent-research/2604.14214-crop/README-en.md) · [Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?](../../../../agent-research/2610.37276-evalalloc/README-en.md) · [Self-Refine](../../../../agent-research/2303.17651-self-refine/README-en.md) · [When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement](../../../../agent-research/2610.36826-ruharness/README-en.md)

### Library admission does not make a strategy the current champion

Strategist turns executable structure, measurement cards, and training-trace experience into cross-task assets, unlike Reflexion's readable lessons. Evaluated nonwinners may remain available for future composition. Selecting the current deliverable separately requires validation and hidden gates, with test data excluded. EvalAlloc governs which evaluation cells receive budget rather than proposing strategy structure. All depend on real execution feedback, but experience accumulation, structural reuse, and budget allocation are distinct mechanisms. Synthetic scores passing any selection rule provide no LLM capability evidence.

Sources: [Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.03618-strategist/README-en.md) · [Reflexion](../../../../agent-research/2303.11366-reflexion/README-en.md) · [Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?](../../../../agent-research/2610.37276-evalalloc/README-en.md)

### Edit lifetime, experience persistence and model internalization are different axes

Strategist accumulates executable reasoning programs and measured experience across tasks. Meta² instead transfers frozen evolution knowledge while keeping realized edits task-local. Continual AutoResearch separates first-solution quality, search utility and final choice: finding a 0.8 candidate sooner but selecting 0.5 is not a final improvement. RSI-Dojo changes a further axis, model-weight learning, so a threshold filter or unexecuted environment registration does not complete training. Compare methods only after fixing retained state, edit scope and feedback timing.

Sources: [Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.03618-strategist/README-en.md) · [Meta²: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.05139-meta-square/README-en.md) · [From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks?](../../../../agent-research/2611.05108-continual-autoresearch/README-en.md) · [Training LLM Agents to Automate LLM Post-Training with RSI-Dojo](../../../../agent-research/2611.03698-rsi-dojo/README-en.md)

### Persisting an environment, evolution guidance and session experience are distinct interventions

EnvOpt retains an environment representation that can serve different queries. It requires lower cost and proxy preservation in training, then rolls back on validation regression. Meta² retains frozen evolution guidance while concrete harness edits apply only to the current run. Continual AutoResearch matches task streams to measure the effects of session and workspace state, separating search speed from final selection. Track edit scope, validation access and what persists across tasks; cheaper trajectories do not establish stronger model capability.

Sources: [EnvOpt: Automated Optimization for Agent Environments](../../../../agent-research/2611.07372-envopt/README-en.md) · [Meta²: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.05139-meta-square/README-en.md) · [From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks?](../../../../agent-research/2611.05108-continual-autoresearch/README-en.md)

### Average validation gain, boundary risk and formal specifications provide different admission evidence

PASE retains skill-program patches on independent validation improvement. FGSE additionally bounds falsification failures and archived damage to avoid hiding dangerous subgroups behind average gains. Verified Quantum Wiki requires independent proofs against frozen specifications before cost/size comparison. These gates provide different guarantees: AST syntax, empirical probes and formal theorems are not interchangeable. The local CPU components neither generate candidates nor perform external verification; test scores and synthetic receipts are contract controls only.

Sources: [Program-Aided Patchable Skill Evolution](../../../../agent-research/2611.14019-pase/README-en.md) · [When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.14326-fgse/README-en.md) · [Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI](../../../../agent-research/2611.09822-verified-quantum-wiki/README-en.md)

### Output exceptions and program patches require different admission evidence

PASE proposes a program patch within a skill/program pair and accepts only strict held-out validation improvement. Agent Gym preserves reversible business exceptions outside the acting agent and still requires expert approval after target/collateral checks. Syntax, matching, authorization, and measured task performance are different judgments. Both local implementations are L1 admission/transaction kernels, not autonomous rule invention, improved model intelligence, or complete RSI.

Sources: [Agent Gym: A Framework for Continuous Evaluation and Evolution of LLM Agents Through Human-in-the-Loop Feedback](../../../../agent-research/2608.15591-agent-gym/README-en.md) · [Program-Aided Patchable Skill Evolution](../../../../agent-research/2611.14019-pase/README-en.md)

### Bounded research expansion and evidence integrity need separate acceptance gates

ScientistTwo organizes research through subset-to-full escalation, successful and failed history, untried seeds, strict-improvement replacement and review budgets. ScientistOne's CoE targets score recomputation, citations, rules and method/code consistency, while its local kernel also externalizes semantic judgments. Even unanimous stage acceptance and high review scores can rest on incorrect or fabricated logs. Conversely, recomputable evidence does not establish novelty or superiority. Local state tests establish budgets and data flow, not capability on the 107 research tasks.

Sources: [ScientistTwo: Pioneering the Human Knowledge Frontier with Autonomous AI](../../../../agent-research/2609.19644-scientist-two/README-en.md) · [ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence](../../../../agent-research/2605.26340-scientist-one/README-en.md)

### Agent execution layers and environment practice layers need separate ablations

Harness² compares tools, prompts, memory and scripts under the same model/environment and accumulates evidence about improvement. EnvHarness changes practice conditions to expose particular weaknesses while retaining base goal verifiers. Changing both obscures attribution. A serial Chain's conjunction does not establish semantic compatibility; blocking shortcuts does not establish transferable learning. Full EnvRigger requires fresh-rollout acceptance and testing on untouched tasks, a capability chain absent from local wrappers.

Sources: [EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning](../../../../agent-research/2608.19880-envharness/README-en.md) · [Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World](../../../../agent-research/2610.14224-harness2/README-en.md)

### Targeting an influential component differs from allocating budget across branches

MLE-STAR uses executed ablations to focus local plans on a block. MARS schedules modular candidates with budget-aware MCTS and converts code/result differences into transferable lessons. Local impact and performance/time tradeoffs can complement each other but are not one score. Neither paper's competition results validate an empty local controller. Generated scripts, orchestration source, and executed capability are distinct assets.

Sources: [MLE-STAR: Machine Learning Engineering Agent via Search and Targeted Refinement](../../../../agent-research/2506.15692-mle-star/README-en.md) · [MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research](../../../../agent-research/2602.02660-mars-research/README-en.md)

### Discovering a better object differs from grounding research claims about it

AlphaEvolve searches using task-specific executable feedback. ScientistOne additionally checks numerical recomputation, citation support, and method/code alignment. A construction verifier establishes only its checked property, not every claim in a generated paper; a reliable evidence chain also does not guarantee novelty. Official result notebooks cannot recover the original discovery process, so the local contribution remains a cost-reviewed reference.

Sources: [AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery](../../../../agent-research/2506.13131-alphaevolve/README-en.md) · [ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence](../../../../agent-research/2605.26340-scientist-one/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### How do three revisions of one answer and recording a lesson for another attempt distinguish Self-Refine from Reflexion? {#cross-revision-versus-episodic-learning}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Self-Refine generates feedback and edits the current draft, mainly changing that artifact. Reflexion turns execution evaluation into experience readable by the next trial's actor. Both can use a frozen model and imply no gradient training. Check whether feedback enters later context, applies to the new state, and actually improves a verified result; iteration count does not establish learning.

    **Illustrative example:** Correcting a wrong number is a current revision. Saving 'check source tables before quoting numbers' for future tasks is cross-trial state.

    Sources: [Self-Refine](../../../../agent-research/2303.17651-self-refine/README-en.md) · [Reflexion](../../../../agent-research/2303.11366-reflexion/README-en.md)

### Why aren't retaining low-scoring Agent S4 descendants and rejecting non-improving RSIFlow candidates contradictory? {#cross-population-versus-current-parent}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** They maintain different search states. The Agent S4 population retains exploration sources, and low-scoring descendants may help later search; private validation chooses parents. RSIFlow tests each candidate from a frozen parent and failure leaves the next starting state unchanged. One preserves diversity and the other governs the current version. Archive admission is not release, and neither needs the same monotonicity criterion.

    **Illustrative example:** An interface variant with a new action can remain in S4 despite a low score. After a non-improving workflow patch, RSIFlow starts again from the original workflow.

    Sources: [Evolving Agent Interfaces](../../../../agent-research/2610.28601-agent-s4/README-en.md) · [RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent](../../../../agent-research/2610.21791-rsiflow/README-en.md)

### Why doesn't a paired local behavior gain in HarnessLens replace AgentX production-release judgment? {#cross-local-admission-versus-production}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Local validation asks whether the selected behavior gains positively and attributably. Deployment also involves business distributions, guardrails, and actual resources. AgentX can veto a primary gain and records positive and negative experiments. The stages can connect, but small local protocol success supplies neither traffic causality nor authorization to release.

    **Illustrative example:** Offline recovery may improve while request latency rises in production. Functional evidence can hold and guardrails can still reject release.

    Sources: [Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification](../../../../agent-research/2608.27311-harnesslens/README-en.md) · [AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems](../../../../agent-research/2606.26859-agentx/README-en.md)

### Why doesn't RuHarness resample novelty and redundancy with each Dirichlet draw? {#cross-oct29-method-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** They describe overlap of fixed trajectory sets, not six-cell outcome probabilities. Randomizing them changes the uncertainty model. A conservative posterior quantile also does not show that actual agents improved.

    **Illustrative example:** Two criteria flag the same failure set. Sampling a success/failure probability should not change that overlap.

    Sources: [Self-Refine](../../../../agent-research/2303.17651-self-refine/README-en.md) · [When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement](../../../../agent-research/2610.36826-ruharness/README-en.md)

### Why can't one correction-success metric summarize CROP and Self-Refine even though both revise text from feedback? {#cross-crop-prompt-versus-current-answer}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Self-Refine mainly revises the current answer. CROP changes system prompts offline and selects evaluated candidates using accuracy and CoT-normalized output-token cost. A better current answer does not demonstrate prompt transfer; shorter prompts do not ensure shorter or correct answers. Real LLM callbacks and independent validation are additional evidence.

    **Illustrative example:** Correcting one arithmetic answer and finding a concise prompt for unseen arithmetic are different tests. The last newly written prompt cannot be called best before evaluation.

    Sources: [CROP: Token-Efficient Reasoning in Large Language Models via Regularized Prompt Optimization](../../../../agent-research/2604.14214-crop/README-en.md) · [Self-Refine](../../../../agent-research/2303.17651-self-refine/README-en.md)

### Why are neither high EvalAlloc predicted fitness nor high RuHarness criterion utility actual agent success rates? {#cross-evalalloc-fitness-versus-rubric-frontier}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** EvalAlloc estimates unobserved SEARCH outcomes against fixed references, retaining observed cells and requiring confirmation. RuHarness estimates conservative diagnostic value of criteria, and candidate harnesses still need independent validation. These govern budgets and criteria, not outcomes of unexecuted tasks.

    **Illustrative example:** If only 20 of 300 items are evaluated, completed mean 0.8 does not mean 240 actual completions. A criterion that covers failures does not solve tasks.

    Sources: [Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?](../../../../agent-research/2610.37276-evalalloc/README-en.md) · [When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement](../../../../agent-research/2610.36826-ruharness/README-en.md)

### How does Strategist retaining failed strategies differ from Reflexion storing lessons and EvalAlloc confirming champions? {#cross-blueprint-archive-versus-current-pick}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Library admission preserves executable structures and measurement cards without adopting them for the current answer. Final selection still requires both splits to win. Reflexion mainly stores readable experience, whereas EvalAlloc controls observations and confirmation rather than generating structure. Structural archives, lessons, and adopted strategies need separate records.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: an expensive voting strategy may remain a component for a future decomposition program, without replacing the current cheaper reference merely because it entered the library.

    Sources: [Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.03618-strategist/README-en.md) · [Reflexion](../../../../agent-research/2303.11366-reflexion/README-en.md) · [Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?](../../../../agent-research/2610.37276-evalalloc/README-en.md)

### Can a shared file index and a tool reminder added after one run fails use the same training-gain table? {#cross-environment-index-versus-in-run-edit}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Not directly. EnvOpt's index changes a shared environment representation and needs validation on tasks not used to propose the edit. Meta²'s reminder is a bounded harness edit for the current run. What transfers is guidance for making edits, not that reminder.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: search tasks can reuse a directory index, but a recovery reminder for one missing permission should not persist in unrelated tasks.

    Sources: [EnvOpt: Automated Optimization for Agent Environments](../../../../agent-research/2611.07372-envopt/README-en.md) · [Meta²: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.05139-meta-square/README-en.md) · [From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks?](../../../../agent-research/2611.05108-continual-autoresearch/README-en.md)

### Can a patch that raises average validation score but breaks old cases pass PASE, FGSE and Verified Quantum Wiki alike? {#cross-risk-gates-versus-validation}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Those two observations do not decide all three. PASE's explicit rule requires strict held-out improvement. FGSE separately checks archived damage and falsification risk and may reject. Verified Quantum Wiki needs specification-bound independent proof and resource improvement, not an average score. Match admission to observable evidence and update scope.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: nine improved tasks can hide one duplicate payment. An average-score gate may pass while a risk gate rejects; the quantum wiki does not use that task-score criterion at all.

    Sources: [Program-Aided Patchable Skill Evolution](../../../../agent-research/2611.14019-pase/README-en.md) · [When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.14326-fgse/README-en.md) · [Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI](../../../../agent-research/2611.09822-verified-quantum-wiki/README-en.md)

### Can SME approval of a correction rule substitute for a program patch's validation improvement, or vice versa? {#cross-cross-rule-governance-versus-program-validation}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. The former authorizes a downstream exception within target/collateral scope; the latter measures a paired program on isolated validation. Their locations and evidence differ, and neither is semantically established by syntax or type checks.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: an emergency-procurement exception may be authorized by a human. A spreadsheet-formula patch needs strictly improved validation. Calling approval a benchmark gain, or using a score gain to authorize policy, confuses evidence.

    Sources: [Agent Gym: A Framework for Continuous Evaluation and Evolution of LLM Agents Through Human-in-the-Loop Feedback](../../../../agent-research/2608.15591-agent-gym/README-en.md) · [Program-Aided Patchable Skill Evolution](../../../../agent-research/2611.14019-pase/README-en.md)

### After strict-improvement comparison and two review rounds, may ScientistTwo skip a ScientistOne-style evidence audit? {#cross-cross-scientist-control-versus-evidence-integrity}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Comparison and review judgments come from external models or people; the control kernel only schedules calls, updates and stopping. Independent score recomputation, split isolation, log provenance and method/code consistency still need checking. A high score does not prove provenance.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: an external comparator returns true based on a copied high score, and the kernel faithfully updates best. Only execution and provenance audits reveal that the score does not belong to the current code.

    Sources: [ScientistTwo: Pioneering the Human Knowledge Frontier with Autonomous AI](../../../../agent-research/2609.19644-scientist-two/README-en.md) · [ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence](../../../../agent-research/2605.26340-scientist-one/README-en.md)

### If both an agent harness and an environment Contract change and success rises, may the gain be attributed to EnvHarness? {#cross-cross-environment-and-agent-harness-attribution}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Fix the policy, task splits and agent execution layer, compare learning/skills from original versus wrapped environments, then evaluate on untouched environments. Fixed toy wrapper tests cover neither learning nor transfer and do not integrate the two systems.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: adding a test tool while blocking direct submission may reduce failures because of either change. Separate controls are needed for attribution.

    Sources: [EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning](../../../../agent-research/2608.19880-envharness/README-en.md) · [Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World](../../../../agent-research/2610.14224-harness2/README-en.md)

### Would MLE-STAR's ablation targeting and MARS's budget reward always choose the same expensive but influential change? {#cross-cross-block-targeting-versus-budget-allocation}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Ablation asks where refinement matters; a budget reward also trades performance against execution time. Neither automatically implements the other's search rule. A combination must separately fix validation and measured cost.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: a preprocessing change gains 0.01 in one hour, while another branch gains 0.008 in one minute. Influence and budget-limited exploration value can differ.

    Sources: [MLE-STAR: Machine Learning Engineering Agent via Search and Targeted Refinement](../../../../agent-research/2506.15692-mle-star/README-en.md) · [MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research](../../../../agent-research/2602.02660-mars-research/README-en.md)

### Why does verifying a published matrix construction establish neither local AlphaEvolve discovery nor complete research integrity? {#cross-cross-discovery-score-versus-claim-grounding}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** It does not execute proposals, archives, or distributed search, and it does not audit all numbers, citations, or prose/code alignment. Evidence supports only the object and property actually checked.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: a valid complex rank-48 construction does not establish rank48 over every field or local rediscovery. Each stronger claim needs separate evidence.

    Sources: [AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery](../../../../agent-research/2506.13131-alphaevolve/README-en.md) · [ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence](../../../../agent-research/2605.26340-scientist-one/README-en.md)
